definitions.explanation: A situation where one person handles work or tasks that typically require multiple people, originally from restaurant industry terminology.

definitions.gloss: solo parenting; single-handedly caring for children
definitions.explanation: When one parent handles all childcare duties alone, without help from a partner.

examples.japanese: ワンオペで{店|みせ}を{回|まわ}すのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Running the store single-handedly is tough.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}は{人手|ひとで}{不足|ぶそく}でワンオペになる。
examples.english: Late at night, due to staff shortage, it becomes a one-person operation.

examples.japanese: バイトが{休|やす}んで、ワンオペで{忙|いそが}しいランチタイムを{乗|の}り{切|き}った。
examples.english: A part-timer was absent, so I got through the busy lunch rush single-handedly.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}はワンオペ{育児|いくじ}だ。
{夫|おっと}が{出張中|しゅっちょうちゅう}で、{今週|こんしゅう}はワンオペ{育児|いくじ}だ。
examples.english: My husband is on a business trip, so this week I'm doing solo parenting.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}ワンオペで{子供|こども}の{世話|せわ}をしていると、{体|からだ}も{心|こころ}も{疲|つか}れてくる。
examples.english: When you're doing solo childcare every day, it wears you out both physically and mentally.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Abbreviation of ワンオペレーション (one operation), from English "one operation."

ORIGIN:
Originated in the fast-food industry to describe shifts where only one employee works. The term gained wider use after media coverage of overwork issues at chain restaurants.

USAGE:
・ワンオペ + noun: ワンオペ{育児|いくじ} (solo parenting), ワンオペ{営業|えいぎょう} (one-person sales)
・ワンオペで〜する (to do ~ single-handedly)
・ワンオペ{状態|じょうたい} (one-person operation state)

SOCIAL CONTEXT:
The term ワンオペ{育児|いくじ} became popular in discussions about working mothers who bear the burden of childcare alone while their partners work long hours. It highlights issues of work-life balance and unequal division of household labor in Japan.

SIMILAR TERMS:
・{一人|ひとり}で{回|まわ}す - to run (something) by oneself
・{孤軍奮闘|こぐんふんとう} - fighting alone
